newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Bonn, eastern states to split debt repayment.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bonn, eastern states to split debt repayment.

text.p: Germany's federal, state and local governments have reached a compromise on repayment of 8.4 billion marks ($5.5 billion) in communist-period east German debt, Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said on Wednesday.

The principal will be absorbed by the federal government's standing programme for servicing east German debt, while the 630 million marks in annual debt service payments will be shared equally by Bonn and the east German states.

The simmering stand-off boiled up a year ago when Bonn, which has funnelled over one trillion marks in subsidies to the east in the six years since unification, demanded repayment of the old loans, originally disbursed by East Berlin to local councils for schools, sports facilities and other projects.

The eastern governments resisted, saying Bonn had forgiven other debts that predate unification. The councils had had little choice in whether they wanted the original projects, and claimed the debts might never have had to be repaid if Germany had not been reunified.

Both sides claimed to be satisfied with the compromise, but the opposition Greens party said the eastern states had achieved nothing in the year-long stand-off and were now unfairly being made to repay debts they should not owe.

"This agreement leads to the fear that funds urgently needed for the reconstruction of the east will now be wasted on servicing dubious old debts," said Werner Schulz, the Greens' parliamentary business manager.

The federal government pledged it would not finance its portion of the debt repayment to the detriment of the eastern states but at least one member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition put further subsidies in question.

"We must review further whether part of the financing could be made through a reduction of federal transfers to the new (eastern) states," said Ina Albowitz, Schulz's counterpart in the Free Democratic Party, Kohl's junior coalition partners.
The eastern states said they would present within one month a plan on how they would finance their share of the interest.
Reinhard Hoeppner, prime minister of Saxony Anhalt, said, "Our initiative has paid off. ... Bonn has recognised that the old debts are really debts of the (defunct) East German government."
